## Plan

- `ops/lb_routes.toml` — the committed `sig.lb-routes/1` declaration: the
  apex matcher's path rules (`/v1`,`/v1/*` → api backend, enabled;
  `/intake`,`/intake/*` → `sig-intake`, `enabled=false`) plus the
  service/NEG/backend names and the composed-edge upstream each maps to.
- `ops/src/ops/lb_routes.py` — parse/validate the declaration;
  `render_urlmap` merges enabled rules onto a live URL-map export into the
  deterministic import document; `diff_urlmap` reports drift; `render_edge`
  emits the composed edge nginx conf standing in for the LB.
- `sig-ops lb-map plan|render|diff|render-edge`; `sig-ops web-conf` (the
  chrome + terms fragments); `sig-ops route-compare capture|verify` (the
  byte-compare dark check over `ops/public_routes.toml`).
- `ops/gcp/lb-routes.sh` — the L2 leg: prestate (url-maps export + service
  describes + route-compare baseline) → NEG → backend → url-map import →
  poststate verify; `rollback` re-imports the export + deletes the unused
  resources; window guard exit 42 ≥2026-10-13T12:00Z outside 03:00–10:00Z
  (`SIG_LB_NOW` test override); `--check` default needs no ADC/network.
- `ops/gcp/web-roll.sh` — the L1 leg: prestate (describe + baseline) →
  `web.sh --apply all` → poststate (digest + byte-compare). Same guard.
- `ops/web/nginx.conf` — `include /mnt/sig-web/conf/chrome_*.conf;` +
  `include /mnt/sig-web/conf/terms_*.conf;` inside the server block.
- `ops/Dockerfile` — CMD appends `--release-registry
  /mnt/rel/registry` when the mount is present (absent ⇒ unchanged
  behaviour). No `/v1/health` alias: the existing contract
  (`tests/api/test_api_resilience_and_search_bounds.py:305`) requires
  `/v1/health` to stay ABSENT — the L2 probe instead discriminates on the
  answer's SHAPE (the API's JSON 404 on `/v1/health`, vs nginx's HTML 404
  page that the un-routed posture serves).
- `ops/docker-compose.yml` — a `serving` profile: `web` (the real
  `ops/web/Dockerfile` image over `$SIG_SITE_ROOT`), `api` (the real
  `ops/Dockerfile` image over `$SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY` → `/mnt/rel/registry`,
  read-only), `intake` (same image, `serve-intake`,
  `SIG_INTAKE_ENABLED=1`, non-operational), `edge` (`nginx:1.27.5-alpine`
  with the committed `ops/edge.conf` generated by `lb-map render-edge`).
- `ops/README.md` — the runbook note: how a withdrawal takes effect
  (the include is read at nginx start → a roll or `nginx -s reload` is
  needed), the fragment-activation story, the registry-mount production
  command (owed to P34.46/P35.57's roll).

## Self-review / gap analysis vs contract

Two passes: a mechanical re-read of every diff, then the per-AC table below.
Findings closed in-run:

1. **`${VAR:?}` interpolation broke `sig-ops up`/`down`** — the compose
   `serving` profile initially guarded `SIG_SITE_ROOT`/`SIG_RELEASE_REGISTRY`
   with `:?`, but `docker compose` interpolates the whole file for ANY
   command, so every compose call without the vars failed. Fixed to
   `:-` defaults mounting a visible-empty dir; `docker compose config`
   verifies the profile-free parse.
2. **`curl -f` suppressed the 404 body** in `lb-routes.sh` verify — the
   discriminant IS the API's JSON 404 body on `/v1/health` (the API
   deliberately has no `/v1/health`; the existing contract test pins its
   absence). `-sS` without `-f` captures it.
3. **`diff_urlmap` unhashable set** — `paths not in {set(...)}` threw
   `TypeError`; rewritten as an `any()` over set equality.
4. **`pip install uv` unpinned** — the ops image build failed outright when
   PyPI's uv (0.12.23) failed the repo's `required-version = ==0.12.6`
   check. Pinned `uv==0.12.6` in `ops/Dockerfile` (pre-existing fragility
   this ticket's first image build exposed).
5. **`/v1/health` alias reverted** — `tests/api/test_api_resilience_and_
   search_bounds.py` pins `"/v1/health" not in paths`; the L2 probe
   discriminates on answer SHAPE (JSON vs the nginx HTML 404) instead.
6. **mypy narrowing** — `_fail` marked `NoReturn`; the `apex` matcher
   annotated `dict | None`.
7. **`pg_isready` passed during initdb** — the db healthcheck ran
   socket-only inside the container, so compose marked `db` healthy while
   the bootstrap server still wasn't listening on TCP; sqitch then hit
   connection-refused (exit 2) and `service_completed_successfully` failed
   the whole profile. Fixed with `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1` (TCP-only —
   unhealthy until the real listener is up).
8. **edge pinned dead upstream IPs** — a static `proxy_pass
   http://api:8080` resolves once at nginx start; a recreated upstream's
   new IP left the edge proxying into connection-refused 502s for the
   rest of its life (the deterministic flake in the first e2e attempts).
   `render_edge` now emits `resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=10s` + `set
   $sig_upstream …; proxy_pass http://$sig_upstream;` so upstreams
   re-resolve per request — verified live in the composed stack.
9. **`proxy_http_version` at server level is inert under variable
   proxy_pass** — the composed edge proxied upstream over HTTP/1.0, which
   silently disabled the web nginx's gzip (gzip requires HTTP/1.1+).
   Emitted per-location instead (verified: web logs HTTP/1.1, 440→73
   bytes gzipped through the edge).
10. **profile-scoped services survive a profile-less `down`** —
    `docker compose down -v` without `--profile serving` leaves the
    profile's containers running (the edge survived two teardowns, still
    serving the stale-IP conf). The e2e fixture passes `--profile serving`
    on both downs.
11. **gzip fixture under the floor** — the staged `robots.txt` was 24 B,
    below `gzip_min_length 256`; padded past the floor so the gzip
    assertion exercises the real path.
